goal: Recover a reference-grounded HBB DNA-to-RNA-to-protein model, identify the information lost by coarse clinical labels, and generate discriminating questions for independent evidence.
scope: Computational and descriptive research on public HBB reference sequences and an already explored ClinVar snapshot. No new biological mechanism or prospective predictive performance is claimed.

evidence_policy.current_fixture: Exploratory/development data: all 54 source records and the former heldout partition have been inspected.
evidence_policy.validation: A new independent assay/cohort and frozen protocol are required before predictive or discovery claims.
evidence_policy.formal_scope: Reference reconstruction, translation and logical implications can be checked; empirical premises and molecular phenotypes are not established by those checks.

hypotheses.question: Does the GRCh38 minus-strand exon model reconstruct NM_000518.5 and NP_000509.1 exactly, and map the known HbS/HbC DNA controls to the expected protein substitutions?
assumptions: GRCh38 NC_000011.10 and the named transcript/protein are the intended reference versions.
Coordinates are zero-based half-open; exons are reverse-complemented and joined in transcription order.
The standard nuclear genetic code and Met-inclusive protein numbering are used.
hypotheses.expected_observation: A 628-nt spliced transcript, 444-nt CDS including termination codon, and 147-aa protein match the frozen references; c.20A>T gives p.Glu7Val (HbS), and c.19G>A gives p.Glu7Lys (HbC).
hypotheses.falsifier: Any reference-base, reconstructed sequence, transcript/CDS length, protein sequence, or expected control amino-acid mismatch falsifies the implementation/reference-consistency claim.

available_evidence.description: Frozen GRCh38/UCSC/NCBI reference bundle and reconstruction checks.
Reviewed UniProt P68871 sequence, removed initiator Met, and HbS/HbC annotations.

missing_evidence: Reference sources can share RefSeq ancestry; matching them is not independent biological replication.
A correctly mapped protein substitution does not measure polymerization, oxygen affinity, RNA processing or clinical outcome.
hypotheses.discriminating_next_evidence: Use an independently curated sequence/control set to challenge mapping, and independently measured molecular endpoints to test any downstream functional prediction.

hypotheses.question: Which independently recomputed sequence consequences agree with the frozen ClinVar transcript annotations, and which variants retain additional untested RNA or regulatory mechanisms?
assumptions: Comparisons refer to the same transcript version and the same allele orientation.
The toolkit's coarse consequence groups and ClinVar source groups have an explicitly recorded mapping.
Concordance is evaluated without using source consequences to calculate codons.
hypotheses.expected_observation: Computable coding changes have reproducible reference/alternate codons and amino-acid changes. Noncoding or splice-proximal variants remain unresolved downstream, even when their coarse source group agrees.
hypotheses.falsifier: A coding source annotation incompatible with the independently translated codon under the same transcript falsifies concordance and must be reviewed rather than silently reclassified. A claim that all intronic or synonymous variants lack downstream effects is also invalidated by known splicing mechanisms.

available_evidence.description: Hash-pinned 54-record source snapshot and versioned assertions.
Primary evidence that an intronic point mutation can create an additional splice site.
Evidence that RNA fate is context-dependent and not fully determined by a simple consequence class.

missing_evidence: No comprehensive allele-matched RNA isoform, transcript abundance, protein quantity or functional-assay coverage is available for all 54 assertions. The separately integrated reporter assay has two exact allele overlaps; that endpoint is not endogenous HBB expression or protein physiology.
Alternative transcripts, disease/zygosity-specific contexts and regulatory haplotypes are not comprehensively modeled.
The explored fixture cannot serve as untouched validation for revised annotations or predictors.
hypotheses.discriminating_next_evidence: Freeze transcript-specific variant/RNA assay pairs from an independent source and compare predicted coding and splice-context features with measured isoforms and abundance.

hypotheses.question: Do c.327C>A and c.327C>G encode the same p.Asn109Lys substitution, while remaining distinct DNA assertions rather than independent functional replications?
assumptions: Both alleles use NM_000518.5 and the reference codon at c.325_327 is AAC.
Only the directly translated protein change is being compared.
Equivalent translated protein sequences do not imply equivalent RNA processing, abundance, linked haplotype or organism phenotype.
hypotheses.expected_observation: AAC becomes AAA or AAG; both translate Asn109 to Lys. The two DNA allele identities remain distinct and occur at the same locus, so they stay in the same dataset partition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Different translated residue changes under the same reference falsify the codon-equivalence claim. Independent RNA measurements showing different processing or expression would falsify any stronger claim of complete molecular equivalence, but not the narrow translation result.

available_evidence.description: VCV003336287.4 and VCV004847669.1 report the two DNA alleles and the same protein change.
Reference codon reconstruction without clinical-label inference.
Primary bibliographic report identifies Presbyterian as a low-oxygen-affinity variant.

missing_evidence: Study/cohort independence of the two clinical submissions.
Allele-specific RNA, abundance, splicing and haplotype measurements.
Direct biochemical measurements for each exact submitted DNA allele.
hypotheses.discriminating_next_evidence: Compare independent transcript and protein measurements for the two DNA alleles while preserving their distinct sequence and haplotype identities.

hypotheses.question: Is c.92G>T / p.Arg31Met a coding substitution at an exonic splice boundary, and could an additional RNA-processing effect distinguish it from a protein-only explanation?
assumptions: The first coding exon contributes 92 nt, so intron 1 interrupts codon 31 after two bases.
An exonic splice-proximity flag is a candidate feature, not proof of a splice defect.
Any measured effect must be interpreted in a relevant erythroid context and under a named transcript/haplotype.
hypotheses.expected_observation: Reference projection places c.92 at the last coding base of exon 1, and the spliced codon translates Arg31 to Met. The variant should retain both coding and exonic-boundary context; a possible additional splice effect remains unresolved.
hypotheses.falsifier: A reference projection away from that exon boundary or a different translated change falsifies the computational premise. For the biological extension, sufficiently sensitive matched RNA observations showing unchanged isoform use and abundance would argue against an additional splice-processing explanation in that context.

available_evidence.description: Exon coordinates, coding-phase reconstruction and codon mapping.
VCV003766927.1 reports c.92G>T / p.Arg31Met as a likely-pathogenic clinical assertion.
Established precedent that HBB intronic sequence changes can alter splice-site use; this does not establish the effect of c.92G>T.

missing_evidence: Direct RNA splicing and abundance measurements for c.92G>T in an appropriate model.
A comparison that separates transcript-processing effects from altered-protein effects.
Independent clinical and biochemical characterization with genotype and condition specified.
hypotheses.discriminating_next_evidence: Independent RNA isoform/abundance evidence paired with protein production and behavior for the same allele; no splicing defect is asserted from sequence proximity alone.

hypotheses.question: How much of the reference-defined HBB SNV universe and its mechanistic/evidence-quality diversity is absent from the current fixture?
assumptions: The saturation denominator is the 1608-bp annotated transcript locus, not the whole human genome or the wider genomic reference slice.
Only the three non-reference unambiguous substitutions per position are enumerated.
Computational consequence categories are not counts of validated functional defects.
hypotheses.expected_observation: The locus contains 4824 possible SNVs, including 1332 CDS substitutions and 24 substitutions at canonical intronic splice-core positions. Only 53 of the 54 fixture variants lie within that locus, including 17 coding records; HbS/HbC, annotated heme-interaction His64/His93 substitutions and canonical splice-class source rows are absent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reference-coordinate or allele-set reconciliation yielding a different universe or presence of those controls falsifies these coverage counts. Broad functional-generalization claims are unsupported unless a new independently selected benchmark covers the missing mechanisms.

available_evidence.description: Reference-defined transcript span, exons/CDS and splice boundaries.
The frozen selected variant inventory; one upstream record lies outside the transcript span.
Reviewed heme-binding residues and known HbS/HbC controls.

missing_evidence: Population-representative variants, independently measured molecular effects and structural/CNV/indel coverage.
Independent organization/cohort identities and disease/zygosity-specific phenotype labels.
A prospective evaluation sample whose selection was not informed by the present model or explored labels.
hypotheses.discriminating_next_evidence: Freeze an independently sourced functional benchmark covering several mechanisms and evidence qualities before model selection; report coverage and missingness alongside performance.
